newsitem.title: USA: Calif. insurance chief objects to Prudential deal.
newsitem.headline: Calif. insurance chief objects to Prudential deal.

text.p: California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush filed an objection on Thursday to the proposed settlement of a class action lawsuit filed against Prudential Life Insurance Co.
Quackenbush said in a statement that his objections to the class action settlement centered on the process proposed for settling claims against the company.
"In my judgement, the proposed settlement places too much burden on Prudential's customers to prove that fraudulent misrepresentations were made when they purchased their policies," Quackenbush said.

To obtain maximum compensation under the proposed alternative dispute resolution (ADR) plan, the policyholder must generally provide written documentation that he or she was lied to, or the agent must admit to the deception.
In his objection, Quackenbush said agents who intentionally lie rarely leave written evidence behind and face the loss of their jobs if they admit to lying.

Quackenbush said he also objected to the settlement because the ADR does not guarantee full compensation for victims even when there is evidence that similar complaints have been registered against a particular Prudential agent.

"This (proposed settlement) would have the effect of depriving thousands of policyholders of the compensation they deserve," Quackenbush said. "I will not permit Prudential to victimize California consumers again."

Regulators across the United States have accused Prudential of widespread fraudulent sales practices. The settlement could potentially affect 750,000 policyholders in California who may have been victims, Quackenbush said.
